Set the select matrix for a SimInf_model object

Source: R/SimInf_events.R
select_matrix-set.Rd

Replace the select matrix events@E that determines which compartments an event samples individuals from when processing exit, enter, internal transfer and external transfer events. The values in the selected column are used as weights when sampling individuals from the compartments with non-zero entries. The select matrix can be specified as a matrix, or as a data.frame with the columns compartment and select, and an optional column value (default 1); see ‘Arguments’ for details, and SimInf_events for how the select matrix is used when processing events.

Usage

select_matrix(model) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SimInf_model'
select_matrix(model) <- value

Arguments

model

The SimInf_model object to set the select matrix for.

value

The new value for E in the model. E is a matrix to handle scheduled events, see SimInf_events. Each row in E corresponds to one compartment in the model. The values in a column are used as weights when sampling individuals from the compartments with non-zero entries when processing an event. Let s <- select, then the non-zero entries in E[, s] determine which compartments to sample individuals from. This matrix is used for exit, enter, internal transfer and external transfer events. The select matrix E can either be specified as a matrix, or as a data.frame. When E is specified as a data.frame, it must have one column named compartment that defines which compartment is referred to, and one column select that defines the column in E. In addition, the data.frame may contain a column named value with the weight in E (1 if the column is omitted). Note that the data.frame replaces the entire select matrix: entries not included are set to zero, so all columns that the scheduled events refer to must be specified.

Value

The SimInf_model object with the updated select matrix.

See also

select_matrix to extract the select matrix, and shift_matrix to extract the shift matrix. The vignette "Scheduled events" for a tutorial on scheduled events, see vignette("Scheduled events", package = "SimInf").

Examples

## Create an 'SIR' model.
model <- SIR(
  u0 = data.frame(
    S = 100,
    I = 10,
    R = 0),
  tspan = 1:5,
  beta = 0.16,
  gamma = 0.077
)

## Extract the select matrix from the model.
select_matrix(model)
#> 3 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>   1 2 3 4
#> S 1 . . 1
#> I . 1 . 1
#> R . . 1 1

## Change the select matrix so that individuals in the 'I'
## compartment are twice as likely to be selected when
## processing an event with 'select' = 4. Note that the
## data.frame replaces the entire select matrix, so the entries
## in columns 1, 2 and 3 must also be specified.
select_matrix(model) <- data.frame(
  compartment = c("S", "I", "R", "S", "I", "R"),
  select = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4),
  value = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1)
)

## Extract the updated select matrix from the model.
select_matrix(model)
#> 3 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>   1 2 3 4
#> S 1 . . 1
#> I . 1 . 2
#> R . . 1 1
